newsitem.title: USA: Alex. Brown exits corp high-yield business.
newsitem.headline: Alex. Brown exits corp high-yield business.

text.p: Alex. Brown Inc, the retail broker which is set to merge with Bankers Trust New York Corp, said it has elected to exit the corporate bond high-yield business, reducing its role further in the fixed income arena.
"We are out of the corporate high-yield business," said an Alex. Brown spokesman on Tuesday.
Market participants anticipate that Bankers Trust will run the corporate high-yield operations for the newly merged firm.
In addition, Alex. Brown recently announced its departure from the fixed-rate municipal finance business as well.

"We have decided not to continue our present role in fixed income, despite the best efforts of our employees, declining spreads have put pressure on fixed income profitability," said Chief Executive Officer A.B. Krongard in a statement.
About 160 of the firm's 2,700 employees will be affected by the reorganization.

The company said it has reassigned some of its employees to other departments or duties within the company, and is not currently clear how many employees may ultimately lose their jobs due to the reorganization.
In April, Alex. Brown and Bankers Trust announced their agreement to merge in a stock deal valued at about $1.7 billion.

The companies said the combined firms would benefit their clients through Bankers Trust's expertise in syndicated bank lending and high-yield bonds and Alex. Brown's strength in equities research and underwriting.
Bankers Trust is the seventh largest U.S. banking company with assets of $120 billion and has offices in more than 55 countries.

Baltimore-based Alex Brown was established in 1800 and is the oldest investment banking firm in the United States. The firm said it will continue to market variable rate products and aggressively engage in the convertible debt business.
The merger between the two firms is expected to be completed by the fourth quarter.
